To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The influence of a wide range of major life events on residential mobility is not well understood and has not been fully investigated in previous research.
the occurrence of life changing events is associated with residential mobility.

1) most life events increase the odds of moving, even when accounting for the individual’s socioeconomic and demographic characteristics; 2) the odds of moving increase following the occurrence of life event, even when accounting the individual’s attitudes towards their neighbourhood; and 3) the odds of downward and upwards mobility are not significantly different following the occurrence of a life event.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the timing of life events affects the likelihood that people move home, how the likelihood of moving varies across different types of events and how these patterns vary across different groups in society.
the influence of major events on residential mobility.
the influence of major, negative life events on the residential mobility of families.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
life events have an important influence on mobility and neighbourhood transitions, and that this influence is likely to be stronger than previously suggested in the literature.
life events do not drive mobility, and that mobility is a random process.
major life events are a key factor in residential mobility and that this is a key driver of the neighbourhood transitions that occur throughout the life course.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
life events have a strong effect on the likelihood of moving and the direction of moves, but that the impact of these events is not uniform across the population.
life events are important drivers of residential mobility.
we have shown that life events are important predictors of residential mobility and that this mobility is not random.
The main takeaway from our work is that
life events are important for understanding residential mobility.
the influence of life events on mobility is not limited to the most obvious examples, such as the birth of a child.
life events have an important influence on residential mobility, even when controlling for a wide range of individual characteristics.
